query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes is governed by a deformation mechanism involving the formation of adiabatic shear bands, which enhance the penetration properties of the material.
generation.intervention: Variation of temperature and strain rate
generation.mechanism: Formation of adiabatic shear bands, leading to grain refinement and increased dislocation density
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced penetration properties of the material
generation.boundary: Temperature range: -200°C to 500°C, strain rate range: 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between adiabatic shear bands and penetration properties is not well understood and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Compression testing of solidified FeNiCrMn at various temperatures and strain rates, with and without the formation of adiabatic shear bands
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the formation of adiabatic shear bands does not enhance the penetration properties of the material, the hypothesis is falsified

Owing to better practicality and low cost, the AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy, with similar microstructure and properties to the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, was investigated. It is indicated that the AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy consists of the FCC and A2/B2 spinodal decomposition phase and presents better fracture strength and ductility []. In addition, the dynamic mechanical response of HEAs has also received a lot of attention. To use HEAs in extreme industrial environments, there is an urgent need for a comprehensive understanding of their performance and mechanisms during high-speed compression [,,,,]. According to the available literature, in addition to the dislocation-related mechanism, twinning mechanism, grain boundary-related mechanism, diffusion creep mechanism, and dynamic recrystallization mechanism, the shear bands are formed in HEAs at high strain rates or under large deformation conditions [,,,,].
